LESSON: EQUATIONS OF STRAIGHT LINES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra
Topic 2.2: Equations of Straight Lines

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Equations of Straight Lines. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: when x is zero. How do we use gradient or steepness in our daily activities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the gradient in real-life situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Equations of Straight Lines.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Equations of Straight Lines using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss steepness concerning gradient from the immediate environment.
2. Incline a ladder at different positions on the wall to demonstrate change in steepness of gradient. Discuss and compare the positions where the ladder is steeper.
3. Discuss and rewrite the equation of a straight line as y = mx + c. Explain the variables and constants in the equation.
4. Digital Literacy: learner uses digital divices or other resources to explore the steepness or gradient of places.
5. The learner relates the concept of gradient to making work easier in Integrated Science by use of an inclined plane.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Equations of Straight Lines is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
